data.long_meaning: The name Ritu is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ritusamhara', which means 'the collection of seasons'. It is a popular name for girls in India and is often given to mark the onset of a new season or time of year. The name Ritu carries the meaning “Season” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Ritu usually hope their child will grow to embody season and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ritu signifies the continuous cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. It represents the eternal nature of life and the transformative power of change. In Hindu mythology, the goddess Durga is associated with Ritu and is believed to bestow prosperity and good fortune upon those who seek her blessings.
data.etymology: Ritu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Season.”

data.cultural_impact: The name Ritu has deep cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is derived from the Sanskrit word for 'seasons', 'ritu'. Hinduism considers the five seasons - spring, summer, monsoon, autumn, and winter - as the divine aspects of material life, symbolizing renewal, abundance, and transformation. Naming a child Ritu reflects the deep-rooted respect for nature and the belief that the passage of time is marked by the changing seasons.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Ritu has spiritual significance, representing the cyclical nature of time and the universe. Ritu is believed to embody the divine power of transformation, as each season leads to the next, symbolizing rebirth and renewal. The name also reflects the idea that everything in life is connected and interlinked, and that every transition is part of a larger cosmic plan. Additionally, the name Ritu can be seen as a reminder of the importance of living in harmony with nature, and of preserving and celebrating the natural world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ritu symbolizes the cyclical rhythm of life, embodied in the changing seasons. It represents the harmony between the natural world and the human spirit, urging us to embrace the transient beauty of existence.

vedic_reference.note: Ritu is a term used in Vedic literature to denote the six seasons: spring (Vasanta), summer (Grishma), rainy season (Varsha), autumn (Sharad), winter (Hemanta), and the post-winter season (Shishira).
